blocks.text: Setting up your Mac for online tutoring

You do not need a dedicated app to be efficient. Use a clean browser profile for your tutoring work. This keeps your bookmarks and extensions separate from your personal life. Install the Google Docs Offline extension if you teach from locations with unstable internet. This ensures you can keep working even if your connection drops.
Essential shortcuts for Google Docs on Mac

Keyboard shortcuts are the fastest way to reduce mouse movement. On your Mac, the ⌘ key is your best friend. Use ⌘ + / to open the full list of shortcuts anytime you forget one. To quickly find a specific menu item, press Option + / and type what you need.
Manage your admin load with Lazur

Tutors often lose hours to repetitive tasks like formatting progress reports or checking document settings. Lazur sits in your Mac notch and listens when you hold the shortcut. You can ask it to explain how to change a page orientation or where to find a specific setting. It keeps your hands on the keyboard while you get the answers you need.

Clear formatting makes your materials easier for students to read. Use styles for your headings. This creates a document outline automatically. You can jump between sections using the outline on the left side of your screen. If you need to include math or science symbols, use Insert > Special Characters to find what you need without leaving your document.

Sharing a document is simple. Click the blue Share button in the top right corner. Set the permission to Commenter if you want students to give feedback without changing your original text. Use the Suggesting mode for grading. This lets you propose changes that the student can review and accept later.

Every Google Doc has a limit of 1.02 million characters. This is plenty for most lesson plans. If you reach the limit, create a new document for the next unit. This keeps your files fast and avoids loading issues during your live sessions.

faq.question: Is there a native Google Docs app for Mac?
faq.answer: No. Google Docs is a web-based service that runs in your browser. You can create a desktop shortcut via Chrome to make it open in its own window.

faq.question: Can I work on Google Docs without internet?
faq.answer: Yes. You must use Chrome or Edge and enable the Google Docs Offline extension beforehand.

faq.question: How do I see my word count in Google Docs?
faq.answer: Press ⌘ + Shift + C to see the word count, character count, and page count of your document.
